title: City-Aware Priority Routing & Surge Degradation Policy
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a practical multi-region routing policy that prioritizes user-facing latency and availability for customers while preventing cross-region thrashing and preserving Dedicated capacity SLAs. This ticket codifies: 1) latency-driven reroute thresholds, 2) geo (city-level) pinning for user sessions, 3) capacity-aware overflow steering and graded degradation, and 4) circuit breaker rules + automatic rollback triggers.

Background: We've observed cases where short-lived cross-region failover causes oscillation (requests bounce between zones), which both increases tail latency and burns cross-region egress. We must support: (a) strong locality—keep requests in customer-preferred region when acceptable latency and capacity exist; (b) opportunistic reroute—move traffic to another region when it yields meaningful latency improvements and sufficient capacity headroom; (c) graceful shedding—when all regions are congested, degrade non-critical work first and maintain SLOs for high-priority routes.

SLO targets (for routing policy decisions):
- Primary SLO: p95 server-side generation latency <= 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) for hosted tier in-region.
- Tail SLO: p99 latency <= 500ms across regions for external API.
- Availability SLO: 99.95% successful inference responses (2xx) per region per week.
- Error budget usage above 25% in a rolling 6h window will force conservative routing (no cross-region failover except for P0 incidents).

Routing rules (high level):
1) Geo pinning: by default, session and user-id are pinned at city granularity to a primary region for 30 minutes of activity (configurable TTL). Pinning preserves affinity for KV caches and reduces cold KV-cache misses.
2) Latency-based opportunistic reroute: eligible requests may be steered to alternate regions only if: (a) median RTT improvement >= 30ms and (b) target region headroom >= 25% capacity (see capacity signals below).
3) Capacity-aware steering: steering decisions consume capacity budget quotas per customer to avoid large customers saturating remote region pools. Each customer has a dynamic overflow budget computed from committed capacity + recent usage.
4) Anti-thrashing hysteresis: once a session is rerouted, it cannot be rerouted again for 120s unless error rate exceeds the circuit-breaker threshold. This prevents flip-flopping between regions.

Capacity signals used by steering logic:
- GPU util (short window 10s, long window 5m). Use 90th percentile of long-window util.
- Request queue length and average queue time (thresholds below).
- Active model concurrency per model variant.
- Recent allocation failures / OOMs in last 5m.

Circuit breakers and thresholds (initial):
- Soft circuit: queue latency > 250ms OR model-specific err+5xx rate > 1.5% sustained for 30s triggers graded load-shedding and redirects non-critical traffic.
- Hard circuit: GPU util > 92% sustained for 60s OR p99 latency > 1s triggers regional circuit breaker: reject new low-priority requests, enable overflow steering at the cluster level, and raise an alert.
- Global emergency circuit: total cross-region success rate drop > 2% in 10m triggers global fallback to local-only routing and disables opportunistic reroutes until manual review.

Load-shedding strategy (order of graceful degradation):
1) Drop/queue low-priority background requests (batch embeddings, non-interactive rerank jobs labeled background).
2) Inject max-token caps for requests with token_count > 1024 for non-enterprise customers.
3) Swap to quantized / smaller model variant automatically when quality delta acceptable for route (configurable model tier mapping).
4) Fail fast with 429 for new sessions when all mitigations exhausted.

Observability and telemetry: routing decisions must be recorded with labels: session_id, user_country, user_city, src_region, dst_region, decision_reason, capacity_signals_snapshot, model_variant. We will add dashboards:
- routing-decision: p50/p95 latency delta distribution for rerouted requests
- region-capacity: per-region GPU util, queue length, headroom over time
- circuit-breaker: count by reason and time to recovery
- customer-overflow: per-customer overflow budget burn rate

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local sim harness to replay production traces (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (internal canary): enable policy for internal traffic and infra customers (10% of internal) behind feature flag (1 week).
- Phase 2 (external canary): 5% of traffic for low-risk customers with compensated SLAs; monitor error budget and e2e latency (2 weeks).
- Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over a week each step with automated rollback if SLO regressions detected.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Pin granularity: city-level chosen to balance KV cache locality vs. cross-city situations inside same region. We may relax to region level after empirical validation.
- Reroute threshold tuning: 30ms median improvement is a heuristic; will tune from traffic replay experiments to avoid rerouting for negligible gains.
- Overflow budget allocation fairness: initial approach is proportional to recent committed usage; could move to priority-weighted allocation for enterprise customers.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Notes / links: Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/0812-Multi-Region-Routing-Policy. Prototype router PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/4291. Sim harness + traces: gs://redwood-prod-replay/multi-region/2026-02. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abcd1234/routing-decision
acceptance_criteria: Unit-tested routing policy with deterministic sim harness and >95% matched decision parity versus design replay for baseline traces
Routing decisions instrumented and visible on dashboards with per-decision metadata
Canary run shows no increase in error budget burn > 5% relative to baseline during 5-day window
Circuit breaker fires and auto-recovery were validated in staging using injected GPU util and queue load tests
Runbook updated and on-call playbook for region circuit trips created and reviewed by SRE
implementation_plan: Phase A: Add capacity signal collectors (queue length, queue time, model concurrency) to routing service (ENG-router).
Phase B: Implement decision engine with pluggable policies and hysteresis parameters behind a feature flag.
Phase C: Expose per-customer overflow budget in billing/usage service and add checks during steering decisions.
Phase D: Add graduated load-shedding handlers to inference gateway and model proxies (fail-fast with 429, token caps, model swap).
Phase E: Telemetry + dashboards + alerts; run internal canary, then external canary and ramp per rollout plan.
